Merill retired the PR Desk (artifact + `maester-pr-desk` skill) on 2026-11-04 because the stage-queue-process loop didn't work: PRs moved between review and processing, so queued decisions went stale. Don't recreate it.

**Why:** He wants PR review to stay in the GitHub flow, with one place to act.

**How to apply:** For "review PR N", give findings and a draft comment in chat; post it to GitHub only after he approves the text. Rulings that still hold:
- Assign the author when a PR waits on them; remove them on approve or merge.
- The main ruleset has `require_last_push_approval`: after Merill pushes to a PR, his approval no longer counts. Prefer asking the author to fix or merge main; push to a contributor's branch only when he asks for that fix.
- Review comments, approvals above all, are short and informal. Don't restate what the author did, and don't say "exactly what I asked for" or "this is exactly the split". A thanks, the verdict and any optional notes are enough.
- CIS checks follow the benchmark's PowerShell audit procedure (scope, values, missing data); quote the audit from `~/Downloads/REDACTED.0.0.pdf` before asking an author to change scope.

Don't ask for "(Preview)" in a Maester test's Title. `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` already marks the test as preview. The agent checks MT.1200–1213 still have it in their titles, but that's legacy and due for cleanup, not the convention to copy. The same goes for their outer try/catch: native tests let the engine handle 403s and errors.

**Why:** On 2026-10-18 I asked the author of PR 2401 (MT.1225) to add "(Preview)" to match MT.1210. That reversed Merill's own 16 Oct review, which had asked for it to be removed. Merill deleted my comment as invalid.

**How to apply:** Before reviewing a PR, read the existing reviews and comments on it, including the maintainer's own, and don't contradict a change they already asked for. Don't treat the agent tests MT.1200–1213 as the pattern for new checks.

Declaring the session the helper avoids is gating on the wrong one. |

**Kept where it is genuinely needed,** since the name decides nothing: `Get-DlpCompliancePolicy`, `Get-DlpComplianceRule`, `Get-LabelPolicy`, `Get-ProtectionAlert` and `Get-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy` are Security & Compliance cmdlets, so `CISA.MS.EXO.8.1`, `8.2`, `8.4`, `16.1`, `17.3`, `CIS.M365.2.4.1`, `3.2.1`, `3.2.2`, `3.2.3` and `3.3.1` are untouched. `CIS.M365.2.4.1` keeps it for `Get-ProtectionAlert` even though two of its three reads are Exchange Online.

## Part 2: the informational stubs

`CISA.MS.EXO.8.3`, `14.4` and `16.2` gated on three services and call nothing. Their whole body is the author's own sentence through `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom`, and the service gate ran ahead of it, so the operator saw a generic not-connected skip instead. They now declare `Service = 'None'`, as `MT.1060` does.

**`CISA.MS.EXO.9.4` is a fourth case of the same shape, not listed in the issue.** Its body only calls `Get-MtLicenseInformation`, which reads `subscribedSkus` from Microsoft Graph, so it declares `Service = 'Graph'` rather than `'None'`.

## What I left alone, on purpose

**The `Graph` declarations.** Several of these tests do not use Graph either, and the same argument applies, but that is a separate sweep: removing it could cut a dependency of a shared helper that this change did not measure. Happy to do it as a follow-up if you want it.

**Part 3, the Copilot Studio family.** The issue is explicit that changing `Service = 'Graph'` to `'Dataverse'` on `MT.1113`–`MT.1122` would not move the gate, because `MaesterServiceRegistry.psd1` gives `Dataverse` a `Probe = 'Graph'`. It also measured that those ten already skip with a clear reason thrown from the test body. That is a registry decision, not a test edit, so it is yours to make.

## Validation

- `NativeTestAttributes`, `NativeTestLint`, `TestAttributes` (the engine's own attribute suite, 171 tests), `RepositoryLayout`: **226 tests, 0 failures**.
- `Golden.Tests.ps1`: **13/13**, and `selection.json` is **byte-identical** after regeneration — the 2.x golden selections are by tag, so no service declaration moves them. Nothing to regenerate.

content.text:
The skip message comes out as raw licence codes, joined with `&`, under the words "one of these". I traced it through the code on main (`Resolve-MtNativePlan.ps1:333-341`). On a tenant that lacks either licence, MT.1181 skips with:

| Where | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| HTML report (`TestDetail.tsx:113`) | **Licence not in the tenant.** This test requires one of these licences: AAD_PREMIUM_P2&AGENT_365. |
| Result text (`ResultDetail.TestResult`) | Skipped. This test requires one of these licences: AAD_PREMIUM_P2&AGENT_365. |
| 2.x-compatible `TestSkipped` code | `NotLicensedEntraIDP2` |

**What the comments covered**

CodeRabbit raised one point: the legacy `TestSkipped` code is always taken from the first licence in the list. So a tenant that has P2 but lacks Agent 365 is still told `NotLicensedEntraIDP2`, which names the licence it does have. Julien agreed this is engine behaviour, not specific to MT.1181. MT.1181 is currently the only built-in test that requires two licences together, and he offered to open an issue after 3.0. Nobody raised how the message reads.

**Problems with the message**
1. **"One of these" is wrong for a combination.** `&` means the tenant needs both licences, and the sentence says the opposite.
2. **Raw service plan names.** `AAD_PREMIUM_P2&AGENT_365` means nothing to most admins. The licence table already has the codes, so the message could say "Microsoft Entra ID P2 and Microsoft Agent 365".
3. **It doesn't say which licence is missing.** `Test-MtLicenseRequirement` already knows which one failed, but it only returns true or false.
4. **The legacy code** is the issue CodeRabbit raised, above.

**My take:** none of this is caused by #2708; the PR just makes it visible for the first time. The fix belongs in `Resolve-MtNativePlan.ps1`: show display names, word an `&` group as "all of", name the missing licence, and take the legacy code from that licence. That's about 20 lines plus a unit test. I'd still merge #2708 as it is and fix the engine in its own small PR. We could add a "let's do this as a separate engine fix" note to the approval.

content.text:
They come from the module's own licence table, written by hand. That's what I told the subagent to do. Nothing in the module has a friendly name today, and Graph's `subscribedSkus` only returns codes and IDs.

I checked where the names could come from first. The website keeps a generated copy of Microsoft's licensing service plan reference (`website/src/data/license-service-plans.json`), and it has a friendly name for every service plan. But the engine shouldn't read website files, and those names are often wrong for Maester's licence codes. Many of the codes accept more than the one plan they're named after:

| Token | Microsoft's plan name | What the token actually accepts |
|---|---|---|
| `AAD_PREMIUM_P2` | Microsoft Entra ID P2 | the same, so the plan name works |
| `AGENT_365` | Agent 365 | the same |
| `AAD_PREMIUM` | Microsoft Entra ID P1 | P1, P2 or Governance |
| `ATP_ENTERPRISE` | Defender for Office 365 (Plan 1) | Plan 1 or Plan 2 |
| `EXCHANGE_S_STANDARD` | Exchange Online (Plan 1) | any Exchange Online mailbox plan |
| `AAD_WRKLDID_P1` | Microsoft Entra Workload ID P1 | P1 or P2 |
| `EXCHANGE_DLP`, `DEFENDER_XDR` | not real service plans | Maester's own groupings |

Using Microsoft's names would tell a tenant with Entra ID P2 that it needs "Microsoft Entra ID P1".

So I sent the subagent this guidance:
- **Where they live:** a hand-written `DisplayName` for each code in `MaesterLicenseTable.psd1`, describing everything that code accepts (e.g. "Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2").
- **Single-plan codes:** keep Microsoft's name, tidied up (e.g. "Microsoft Entra ID P2", "Microsoft Agent 365").
- **A unit test** that fails if any code has no display name.
- **Custom tests** whose licence code isn't in the table still show the raw code, because there's nothing friendlier to show.

It's still working. Once it finishes, we run MT.1181 on jozra.com and elapora.com.

**What the skip message says now for MT.1181**
- **Neither licence:** "This test requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 and Microsoft Agent 365. The tenant has neither."
- **Entra ID P2 only:** "… The tenant does not have Microsoft Agent 365." The 2.x skip code is now `Custom` instead of `NotLicensedEntraIDP2`.
- **Agent 365 only:** "… The tenant does not have Microsoft Entra ID P2."
- **Microsoft 365 E7, or both licences:** the test runs.

The friendly names are hand-written in `MaesterLicenseTable.psd1`, and a unit test fails if any licence code has no name. Two of the longer names may read clumsily inside "requires X and Y": "an Exchange Online licence" and "a Microsoft Defender XDR workload (…)". No current test pairs them with another licence, so it can wait.

    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Turns a Secure Score control name into an instance ID the engine accepts, unique within the family.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Most control names (mdo_safelinks, AdminMFAV2) are valid IDs and are returned unchanged. A character outside
    A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-' becomes '-', leading characters that are not a letter or digit are dropped and
    the result is cut to 128 characters. A name that collides with one already used gets -2, -3... Returns
    nothing for a name with no letter or digit. Adds the returned ID to UsedId.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([string])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyString()] [string] $ControlName,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]] $UsedId
    )

    $id = ($ControlName -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9._-]', '-') -replace '^[^A-Za-z0-9]+', ''

    if ($id.Length -gt 128) { $id = $id.Substring(0, 128) }
    $candidate = $id
    $n = 1
    while (-not $UsedId.Add($candidate)) {
        $n++
        $suffix = "-$n"
        $candidate = $id.Substring(0, [Math]::Min($id.Length, 128 - $suffix.Length)) + $suffix
    }
    $candidate
}

Both fixes are pushed to the contributors' branches. The full unit suite passes on both, and each new test fails on the original code, so they catch the bug.

**#2672 (MT.1264), commit `7a8cc3528`.** A control name that isn't a valid instance ID no longer errors the whole family:
- Characters outside letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` become `-`.
- Leading symbols are dropped and the ID is cut to 128 characters.
- Two names that end up the same get `-2`, `-3`, and so on.
- A name with no letter or digit is skipped.

Every control name that exists today is already valid, so current IDs don't change.

**#2712 (MT.1266), commit `e50565c93`.** The helper now returns the exact percentage, and the test compares that with the target.
- It's computed with `[decimal]`, because with doubles 57 of 100 comes out as 56.99999999999999 and would miss a 57% target.
- The report truncates to one decimal instead of rounding, so 79.96% shows as **79.9%** and never reads as reaching an 80% target.

On #2712, the first full run had one failure in a Zero Trust pack test. Both suites were running on the same machine at the same time and shared a temporary folder. The file passed 43/43 when run alone.

- **Your approval no longer counts on either PR,** because you pushed last. They need another maintainer's approval, or a push from the author.

## Description

This separates result redaction and sensitive configuration handling from #2525 so the shared reporting behavior can be reviewed independently of the GitHub checks.

The optional `Add-MtTestResultDetail -RedactedResult` parameter supplies complete alternative result Markdown for selected redacted outputs. It protects the result Markdown; other fields continue to use the existing generic identity replacement.

The changes cover the following:

- **For exported results:** Prepare detached copies and omit `TestResultRedacted` from saved output, including unredacted JSON and HTML. Caller objects and the result details returned by `-PassThru` retain their original values.
- **For HTML:** Prepare its copy independently from the original results, so HtmlOnly can still select the alternative after non-HTML outputs have been prepared.
- **For imported results:** Use a valid nonblank alternative when available. Invalid alternatives fall back to generic replacement rather than stopping export. That fallback retains the existing best-effort limits.
- **For Markdown failures:** Preserve readable messages from original and deserialized error records, including AllOutputs redaction, without changing JSON or caller records.
- **For sensitive configuration:** Redact complete values marked sensitive in the settings registry, including unused declarations, without changing the configuration used by checks.

When `Description` is omitted, the static result template applies to both result variants. With an explicit description, callers supply complete content for both variants.

Existing parameter binding is preserved. New callers must still supply nonblank Markdown when explicitly using `-RedactedResult`; tolerance for invalid alternatives applies when consuming results.

## Validation

On Linux / PowerShell 7.6.6 / Pester 5.7.1, 70 selected reporting cases passed and three optional XLSX cases were skipped because ImportExcel was unavailable. These cover scoped-result and configuration redaction, HTML, flattening, Markdown failure messages, and independent exports in None, HtmlOnly and AllOutputs modes. Changed-file PSScriptAnalyzer, module build and output validation passed.

The release-version fixtures verify that Markdown displays the release version while JSON retains its version object and `-PassThru` retains its original `[version]` value.

The failure-message regression failed before the fix for deserialized records and for a Pester custom test exported through `Invoke-Maester -RedactUserIdentity AllOutputs`. Both pass after the fix. The fixtures check runtime-generated failure text, multiple error records, redacted JSON and Markdown, and preservation of the original error records returned by `-PassThru`. An additional case verifies that an explicit description bypasses the static template for both result variants.

The full unit-test command completed with 4 failures out of 6,631 tests, all Azure-request URI assertions. A fresh run of that test file on unchanged base `506064a0147a54085f01d00797c169820a709a60` reproduced all four. They are not introduced by this reporting change; the full local suite is not green.

The export fixtures read actual CSV and JUnit/NUnit XML files. XML is checked against the names and outcomes it exports; it does not include result Markdown. XLSX export and read-back previously passed in all three modes with ImportExcel 7.8.10 on the earlier revision; they were not rerun on this revision. The synthetic reporting fixtures make no tenant requests.

The unredacted reports from a combined live build omit alternative result Markdown and mask the sensitive configuration values. Those reports do not contain a source revision and do not exercise live HtmlOnly or AllOutputs exports. They provide supporting integration evidence rather than exact-revision validation of this PR.

## Dependencies

This PR is independent of #2525's setting fixes and #2633. Those three may merge independently; merging #2525 first is recommended. #2635 requires both #2633 and this PR to merge first.

PR #2540 has reconciled this reporting behavior and the other foundations at `e70990fab7c2a2dad034b9840502d89d59d7eab5`. After the prerequisites merge, reconcile the dependent branches against actual upstream main and repeat affected validation.

Current revision: `a04e6ba7558da2e36fc955beeffb509e38d81fc7`. Hosted validation is running on this revision. Maintainer review and approval remain required.

## 📑 Description
Align CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations v7.0.0 recommendations 2.1.8-2.1.10 with their parked-domain audit procedures.

The shared classifier considers a domain non-sending only when it has one SPF v1 record containing a non-authorizing `-all` or `~all` mechanism, with no Exchange DKIM signing configuration and no selector1/selector2 DKIM CNAME or TXT records. It classifies the domain as parked only when there is also no usable MX route (including an explicit null MX of `0 .`) and no A, AAAA, or CNAME record at the apex. Positive sender evidence prevents automatic parked classification. Incomplete or ambiguous evidence remains unknown; when the applicable audit branches differ, the check reports Investigate rather than silently granting the parked exception. `SendingFromDomainDisabled` is not used.

- 2.1.8 requires parked/non-sending domains to end with `-all`; sending-domain SPF records and evaluated redirect targets must end with `-all` or `~all`.
- 2.1.9 requires enabled, valid DKIM for sending domains; parked domains must not publish standard selector1/selector2 DKIM CNAME or TXT records. An Exchange signing configuration alone does not fail the parked audit. A known selector record fails the parked check even if another selector lookup failed; incomplete lookups require investigation only when no selector record is known.

I've posted the 11 author-change comments and assigned each author. #2540 has its taxonomy keys approved, #2637 has a yes on the workflow, and #2694 now says MT.1253 stays a test. I've also saved your rulings to memory.

**Are MT.1253 and MT.1266 ready to merge? Not yet.**
- **#2712 (MT.1266)** has no code problems left. Two things stand in the way:
  - It now conflicts with main in `selection.json`, the golden fixture file. I can merge main and regenerate it, the same way I'm doing for #2607.
  - Another maintainer has to approve it, because my fix made you the last pusher.
- **#2694 (MT.1253/1254)** still needs Eduard to renumber the tests from MT.1267, since MT.1253–1258 are Cloud-Architekt's. MT.1254 also needs to read the newer settings-catalog security baselines, not just the legacy ones.

**#2634 (`-RedactedResult`): I'd accept it.**
- **The problem:** today's redaction is a generic find-and-replace on known user identities. It can't catch things it doesn't know about, like GitHub logins inside a check's own result text.
- **What it adds:** with `-RedactedResult`, the check that built the result also supplies a safe version of it. #2635 and #2540 use it 14 times each for exactly that.
- **The cost:** it's optional and doesn't break existing callers. But it becomes public API that custom tests can call.

If you accept it, I'd add one ask: document it in the writing-tests guide.

**#2673: the parked-domain rules are CIS, but detecting parked domains isn't.**
- **What CIS v7 requires:**
  - 2.1.8: a parked domain must have `v=spf1 -all`.
  - 2.1.9: it must not publish DKIM records.
  - 2.1.10: it must have DMARC `p=reject`.

  So those requirements belong in the checks.
- **What it leaves out:** CIS says "any domain not used for sending email" and never says how to tell which domains those are. Its audit has the auditor run the checks for each domain "that sends email from Exchange Online". Deciding which domains don't send is the auditor's judgement.
- **The PR's 1.5k-line classifier:** it guesses parked domains from DNS records (SPF, DKIM, MX, A/AAAA/CNAME). That's Maester's own inference, not CIS.
- **My recommendation:** the `ParkedDomains` parameter only. By default every custom domain gets the sending rules, and a listed domain gets the parked rules. If you want the heuristic, it should only flag a domain as "looks parked, add it to `ParkedDomains`" and never change the verdict on its own.

**#2688: what "families" means.** A family is one test that produces one result row per item it finds. MT.1024 works like this, with one row per Entra recommendation (`MT.1024.<name>`). Dfrank77 asked whether the risk tests should do the same, with one row per risky user. That would cause two problems:
1. **A clean tenant would look skipped.** With no risky users, a family has nothing to produce rows for, so it reports *Skipped (NoInstances)* instead of *Passed*. The good result disappears.
2. **Noise between runs.** The row IDs come from the users, so rows appear and disappear as people become risky or get remediated. That clutters result comparisons and history.

As single-result tests, each check gives one pass or fail with a table of the risky users, privileged ones listed first. The catch is severity. A single-result native test has one fixed severity, so it can't go to High just because a privileged user is in the list. So: one row per test, privileged principals at the top of the table, no severity raise. That's what my comment on #2688 says.

origin/main:powershell/public/run/Add-MtAffectedObjectFact.ps1:1:﻿function Add-MtAffectedObjectFact {
# Affected objects

Builds a consolidated inventory of all objects ("affected objects") involved in a Maester test run —
Microsoft Entra ID objects, tenant-level configuration surfaces, Microsoft Graph resources,
and external systems such as GitHub. The result is attached to the Maester results object as
the top-level `AffectedObjects` property, written to `<name>-affected-objects.json` (and
`<name>-affected-objects.csv` with `-ExportCsv`), and rendered on the **Affected objects** page of the HTML report.

## Opting in

Collection is off by default: `Invoke-Maester -IncludeAffectedObjects` turns it on and the html
report then offers the **Affected objects** page. The switch sets
`$__MtSession.IncludeAffectedObjects`, which gates the per-test `RelatedObjects` capture in
`Add-MtTestResultDetail`, and is passed to `ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult`, which gates the merge
and the `AffectedObjects` property. A report generated without it carries none of this data (no
`RelatedObjects` on the test results, no affected objects entries in `OutputFiles`) and the report's
sidebar does not offer the page.

`-RedactUserIdentity` needs the inventory to know which values belong to which user, so it
collects one even when `-IncludeAffectedObjects` was not passed. In that case `Invoke-Maester`
removes the `AffectedObjects` property again once the replacement map has been built, so the
report does not grow and the page does not appear unasked.

`Get-MtHtmlReport` embeds a slim copy: per record only `System`, `Type`, `Id`, `DisplayName`,
`PortalLink`, `Tests` and a `Referenced` flag (true when a check pointed at the object rather than
only the request cache), and no `RelatedObjects` on the tests. The JSON output and the objects
files keep the full records.

The page also needs a report template built from current `/report/src`. If
`<name>-affected-objects.json` was written but the sidebar has no Affected objects entry, the check-in
artifact `powershell/assets/ReportTemplate.html` is stale — see the stale template
troubleshooting section in [report/README.md](../../../report/README.md).

## Record schema

Every source normalizes into the same record shape so results can be merged and deduplicated:

| Field               | Description                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `System`            | Where the object lives: `EntraID`, `MicrosoftGraph`, `DefenderXDR`, `ExchangeOnline`, `GitHub`, ...               |
| `AnchorKind`        | How the object is identified — see [Anchor kinds](#anchor-kinds)                                                  |
| `Type`              | Canonical object type (`ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `User`, `Group`, `ServicePrincipal`, Graph resource path, ...) |
| `Id`                | Object id (GUID), resource key (`Fido2`), or external identity (`org/repo`); `$null` for singletons/collections  |
| `DisplayName`       | Human-readable name when the source provides one                                                                 |
| `UserPrincipalName` | UPN of a user object when the source provides one; used by PII redaction                                          |
| `PortalLink`        | Admin-portal deep link when a template exists for the type                                                       |
| `Tests`             | Test ids (`MT.xxxx`, ...) that referenced the object (aggregated)                                                 |
| `Sources`           | Which of the three detection sources found it (aggregated)                                                       |
| `Facts`             | What a pack or test added about the object with `Add-MtAffectedObjectFact` (see [Facts](#facts)); empty if none  |

﻿function Use-MtModuleFunction {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Makes Maester module functions that are not exported callable from a unit test.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Check functions that became native tests are no longer exported (Maester 3.0). For each name this
    defines a global proxy function with the same parameter block, which runs the module's function in
    the module's scope with the bound parameters and forwards pipeline input object by object. Mocks
    with -ModuleName Maester apply.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [string[]] $Name
    )
    $module = Get-Module Maester | Select-Object -First 1
    foreach ($n in $Name) {
        $command = & $module { param($c) Get-Command -Name $c -CommandType Function -ErrorAction Stop } $n
        $metadata = [System.Management.Automation.CommandMetadata]::new($command)
        $binding = [System.Management.Automation.ProxyCommand]::GetCmdletBindingAttribute($metadata)
        $paramBlock = [System.Management.Automation.ProxyCommand]::GetParamBlock($metadata)
        # Proxy with begin/process/end and a steppable pipeline (as ProxyCommand.Create does) so pipeline
        # input reaches the module function once per object instead of only the last bound values.
        $body = @"
$binding
param($paramBlock)
begin {
    `$__mtModule = Get-Module Maester | Select-Object -First 1
    # Resolved in the module's scope, so invoking it runs the function in the module's session state.
    `$__mtCommand = & `$__mtModule { param(`$__mtName) Get-Command -Name `$__mtName -CommandType Function -ErrorAction Stop } '$n'
    `$__mtPipeline = { & `$__mtCommand @PSBoundParameters }.GetSteppablePipeline(`$MyInvocation.CommandOrigin)
    `$__mtPipeline.Begin(`$PSCmdlet)
}
process { `$__mtPipeline.Process(`$_) }
end { `$__mtPipeline.End() }
"@
        Set-Item -Path "function:global:$n" -Value ([scriptblock]::Create($body))
    }
}

content.text:
I found the cause of the lockbox failures, and it isn't the lockbox check. The test runner runs up to eight test files in one PowerShell process and keeps the previous file's Pester result in a variable named `$result`. Variable names ignore case, so a later test that mocks `Add-MtTestResultDetail` and filters on `-not $Result` reads that leftover result object, and the filter fails. That's why the two tests pass on their own and fail in a full run. Any test that filters on `$Path`, `$file` or `$config` could break the same way.

So far the PR has three changes:
- **`Test.MT.1265.md`:** removed the byte order mark.
- **`Invoke-MtEngineRun.Tests`:** `Test-CurrentTest` now declares `[OutputType([string])]`.
- **The runner (`Invoke-PesterTestFile.ps1`):** its variables now start with `__mt` and it removes its parameters before the tests run, so tests can't pick them up.

The full suite is running again to confirm the fix. If it's clean, I'll commit, push and open the PR. Nothing is committed yet.

content.text:
I opened [#2727](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2727) to get main's unit tests passing again, and the full suite passes locally: 8,323 tests, none failing. Before the fix, the same run had 5 failures. CI hasn't started on the PR yet. You opened it, so another maintainer has to approve it before it can merge.

It fixes three things:
- **`Test.MT.1265.md`** had a byte order mark, from #2670. I re-saved it without one.
- **`Test-CurrentTest`** in `Invoke-MtEngineRun.Tests.ps1` returned a string without declaring `[OutputType]`, which failed the PSScriptAnalyzer check twice. It now declares `[OutputType([string])]`.
- **The two CIS 1.3.6 lockbox failures** came from the test runner, not from #2690.
  - `Invoke-PesterTestFile.ps1` runs up to eight test files in one process and kept each file's Pester result in `$result`.
  - PowerShell variable names ignore case, so a later file's mock filter `-not $Result` read that leftover result instead of the parameter, and the filter never matched.
  - The runner now uses `$__mt` names for its own variables and removes its parameters before the tests run.

This was probably also behind failures in other tests that only showed up in a full run. One gap remains: with `pester.ps1 -InProcess`, tests still run under `pester.ps1`'s own variables. The PR notes that it doesn't change that path.
